messages:
kevin: Thinking aloud — we need a lightweight per-org policy that combines RPM/TPM with a small concurrency cap and explicit burst credits. Current hybrid models are messy for billing and console UX.

tara: +1. can you sketch the shape? i care about predictable tail latency more than absolute token volume.

kevin: rough idea: each org gets a base RPM + a burst bucket (token-bucket for short spikes). concurrency cap enforced separately. tiers map to both rpm and concurrency. example config: 

```
org_rate_limits:
  org_id: org_123
  tier: silver
  rpm: 3600        # requests per minute
  tpm: 180000      # tokens per minute (approx) or keep both
  concurrency: 8
  burst_tokens: 120
  burst_window_secs: 60
```

oliver: i like explicit burst_tokens. question: do we make burst consumption visible in console? ops needs it for debugging.

jess: please also add per-route multipliers — embeddings and stream-generation should weigh differently. e.g. embeddings * 1, chat-stream * 3.

kevin: agreed. propose multiplier config + reporting. design note: enforcement points debate — edge (ingress LB) vs request-router.

sam: router-level enforcement is easier to align with routing/routing-policy (fallbacks to cheaper model). edge-level is cheaper for early rejection though.

oliver: performance note: concurrency caps should be applied post-routing (after we know model/variant) so we can prefer cheaper variants under pressure. we can add a pre-check at edge to avoid head-of-line queuing.

kevin: telemetry: we must emit these metrics per org: rpm_used, tpm_used, burst_used, concurrency_inuse, throttle_reasons. dashboard panels: 24h heatmap + recent minute.

jess: rollout idea: start w/ read-only console indicators + sampling-based enforcement (soft reject with header X-Rate-Limit-Warn) for 2 weeks, then strict enforcement for <1% test orgs, then ramp.

ratebot: deploy-check: policy config needs validation: rpm>0, concurrency>=1, burst_tokens<=rpm/2. failing validation triggers config reject.

kevin: open questions: 1) do we keep separate TPM vs RPM or derive tokens from avg tokens/request? 2) grace credits across orgs for failed retries? 3) billing mapping for burst credits.

tara: answers: 1) keep both but derive default TPM = rpm * avg_tokens_estimate (config override allowed). 2) grace credits: prefer short lived credits tied to incident windows, manual grant via support console. 3) bill only for consumed tokens, clearly show burst consumption line-item.

sam: i'll prototype a router hook and expose sample headers (X-Org-Burst-Remaining). i'll also add a small backoff hint header when concurrency blocked.

kevin: action items: @sam prototype router enforcement and headers; @jess spec console UI for burst + per-route multipliers; @tara own rollout plan + telemetry panels; @oliver vet concurrency-alignment with model-routing. i'll collect and turn into a short RFC.

jess: thanks — please include a simple example in RFC showing how a spike moves through burst bucket -> concurrency cap -> fallback model. :thumbsup:

kevin: will do. thanks all.
